title: Turnkey Event Management and Production Services for the American Thanksgiving in Singapore Festival
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice only. The solicitation is not available at this time. Quotations submitted in response to this notice will not be accepted. The U.S. Department of State, U.S. Embassy Singapore, intends to issue a Request for Quotations for turnkey event planning, production, and management services for the inaugural American Thanksgiving in Singapore Festival. The public festival is tentatively planned for November 2026 at Jewel Changi Airport, Level 4. The event will be designed to accommodate an anticipated attendance of at least 1,000 people. It is expected to include multiple activity zones, American corporate partners, exhibitors, entertainment, food and beverage activations, and interactive experiences highlighting American Thanksgiving, American culture, and American food ingredients and products. Scope of Requirement The contractor will serve as the single point of responsibility for the successful planning, coordination, production, execution, and closeout of the festival. The contractor will furnish all personnel, supervision, project management, equipment, materials, supplies, transportation, production services, subcontractors, vendor coordination, licenses, permits, approvals, and other resources necessary to deliver a complete and fully operational event, except for any property, services, facilities, or information expressly identified in the solicitation as Government-furnished. Required services are anticipated to include, but are not limited to: Event concept development, design, and planning Venue and stakeholder coordination Project and production management Staging, audiovisual, lighting, sound, and technical production services Event logistics, setup, teardown, and waste removal Exhibitor, sponsor, vendor, and subcontractor coordination Entertainment and programming coordination Food and beverage activation coordination Marketing and promotional support Registration, attendance, and guest-flow management Health, safety, security, and emergency planning On-site event operations and staffing Required licenses, permits, registrations, and approvals Post-event closeout and reporting On-Site Management and Subcontractor Control The prime contractor must provide active, on-the-ground management in Singapore and retain overall responsibility for all subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers. The prime contractor shall designate an experienced on-site event manager with authority to direct the work, control subcontractor performance, commit contractor resources, resolve operational issues, and coordinate directly with the Contracting Officer�s Representative and other event stakeholders. The on-site event manager must be available in Singapore for required planning meetings, site visits, rehearsals, setup, event execution, teardown, and closeout activities. The event manager must be continuously present at the event site during setup, rehearsals, public operating hours, and teardown. The prime contractor may subcontract portions of the work but may not delegate its overall management, supervision, quality-control, or contractual responsibilities. The prime contractor will remain fully responsible for the performance, conduct, safety, quality, and timely delivery of all work performed by its subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers. The solicitation will require quoters to identify their proposed on-site event manager and provide information concerning the individual�s qualifications, authority, availability, and experience managing comparable events. Quoters will also be required to describe their proposed staffing structure and approach to managing subcontractors and vendors. The final solicitation will contain the complete performance requirements, deliverables, evaluation criteria, quotation instructions, and applicable terms and conditions. Contract and Award Information The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price contract. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and make an award without discussions. Therefore, each quoter should submit its best terms in its initial quotation. Information regarding any pre-quotation conference or site visit, if applicable, will be included in the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quotation in accordance with the solicitation, which the Government will consider. System for Award Management Registration Quoters must have an active registration in the System for Award Management at SAM.gov when submitting a quotation and at the time of contract award. SAM registration is free. Prospective quoters are encouraged to begin the registration process early because registration may take several weeks to complete. Registration assistance is available through the Federal Service Desk. Authorization to Perform in Singapore Because contract performance will take place in Singapore, the contractor must be legally authorized to operate and conduct business in Singapore. The contractor must possess all licenses, permits, registrations, approvals, and professional or technical qualifications required to perform the contract. The solicitation will include Department of State Acquisition Regulation clause 652.242-73, Authorization and Performance (AUG 1999). Under this clause, the contractor will be required to warrant that it: Has obtained authorization to operate and conduct business in Singapore Has obtained all licenses and permits necessary to perform the contract Will comply fully with all applicable Singapore laws, decrees, labor standards, and regulations throughout contract performance If a subcontractor or joint-venture partner will perform any portion of the work, that entity must also satisfy the applicable authorization, licensing, permitting, and legal-compliance requirements. The contractor will be responsible for obtaining and maintaining all required authorizations, registrations, licenses, permits, and approvals at no additional cost to the Government. The apparent successful quoter shall provide evidence of the required business authorizations, licenses, permits, registrations, and technical qualifications upon request by the Contracting Officer and before contract award. Electronic Submission Instructions for submitting quotations electronically will be included in the solicitation. Quotations submitted in response to this pre-solicitation notice will not be accepted. Other Information Prospective quoters may refer to the following Singapore Government resources: Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority: https://www.acra.gov.sg Ministry of Manpower: https://www.mom.gov.sg

description: ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. Evaluation of the capability packages received in response to the Request for Information (RFI-RIKD-19-01) resulted in a determination that a small business set-aside could be established. A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for this effort is anticipated to be released during the 1st quarter of CY 2020. Potential Offerors will be encouraged to review and comment on the Draft RFP, including the Statement of Work (SOW) and Sections L and M. Please monitor this notice for updates. title: Senior Procurement Executive Message to the Department of State Contractor and Federal Assistance Community on the Lapse in Appropriations
description: Senior Procurement Executive Message to the Department of State Contractor and Federal Assistance Community on the Lapse in Appropriations As the Department�s Senior Procurement Executive, I am reaching out to share guidance due to the lapse in appropriations that occurred on October 1, 2025. This guidance relates to the handling of Department, including US Agency for International Development (USAID), contract and federal assistance (grants) awards, that is consistent with Department and Office of Management and Budget�s Guidance on Operations During a Lapse in Appropriations. The Antideficiency Act prohibits agencies from incurring obligations that are in advance of, or that exceed, an appropriation, with certain limited exceptions. As you are aware, a fiscal year 2026 appropriation is not yet enacted. For many Department accounts, this results in a lapse in funds designated to purchase certain supplies and services and issue grants and reduces the Department�s capacity to provide oversight on contracts and grants. As a result, certain planned procurements and grants may be cancelled, or postponed, and certain existing contracts and grants may be stopped, suspended, reduced in scope, or terminated. Additionally, payments may be delayed. If the lapse directly affects a contract or grant, on or about October 1, 2025, the Department�s contracting officers and grant officers will notify contractors and recipients of the status of their contract or grant. If a contract or grant will not be affected at the onset of the lapse in appropriations, the Department does not plan to provide any separate notifications or communications of that fact. Unless the contracting officer or grants officer provides a formal notification to the contrary, all Department contractors and recipients must continue to comply with all terms, conditions, requirements and deliveries specified in their contracts or grants. Once a Continuing Resolution or full-year appropriation is signed into law, the Department will begin implementing the plan to orderly resume activity and will notify contractors/recipients at that time. Thank you for your continued partnership with the Department, and for your cooperation as we work together to manage this lapse in appropriations.

title: Responses to Vendor Questions � RFQ 19NL8026Q0007 MSG Cook Services, The Hague, The Netherlands
description: "SEE ATTACHED" Responses to Vendor Questions � RFQ 19NL8026Q0007 MSG Cook Services, The Hague, The Netherlands Notice: Close of Question Period Issued: August 10, 2026 at 12:45 hours (local time) The Government thanks all prospective Offerors for their thoughtful questions regarding RFQ 19NL8026Q0007, MSG Cook Services, The Hague, The Netherlands. The responses below represent the Government's final answers to all questions received to date. Please be advised that the question period for this solicitation is now closed, and no further questions will be accepted. Offerors should rely on the solicitation package, as clarified by this Q&A document, in preparing their final quotations. Quotations remain due by August 20, 2026, at 1700 hours (local time), submitted electronically to TheHagueContracts@state.gov in accordance with the instructions in the solicitation letter and Section 3. The Government appreciates the diligence shown by all prospective Offerors in preparing thorough, well-informed submissions. Page references to the solicitation package (RFQ 19NL8026Q0007) are provided beneath each response for traceability. Question 1 � Availability of Kitchen Photographs, Floor Plan, and Government-Furnished Property Inventory (Rephrased from: "Would the Government kindly provide photographs, a floor plan or dimensions of the MSGR kitchen and dining areas...") The Government is unable to provide photographs, floor plans, or dimensions of the MSGR kitchen and dining areas due to security concerns associated with the Marine Security Guard Residence (MSGR). The pre-quotation site visit scheduled for August 5, 2026, per Provision 52.237-1 (Site Visit), did not take place, as no prospective Offerors expressed interest in attending. Offerors must rely on the written description provided in the solicitation, including the Government Furnished Property/Equipment inventory at Attachment 2 ("all cooking pots, pans, and kitchen utensils and equipment as per attached"), together with the Performance Work Statement, to assess equipment adequacy for proposal purposes. Solicitation citations: Attachment 2 (Government Furnished Property), page 28; Section 3, Provision 52.237-1 (Site Visit), page 47. Question 2 � Minimum Staffing Requirements for the MSG Detachment Cook Position (Rephrased from: "Does the Government anticipate service being delivered by a single on-site cook...or is additional support staff...expected or permitted...") The Performance Work Statement identifies the MSG Detachment Cook as the sole Key Personnel position (Section 4.5.1). The Contractor is responsible for furnishing "all managerial, administrative, and direct labor personnel that are necessary to accomplish the work" under the contract (Section 1.0, Scope of Work). The Government does not mandate a specific staffing structure; Offerors may propose additional support staff (e.g., a kitchen helper) as needed to fully meet the requirements within their firm-fixed monthly price. Solicitation citations: Section 1.0 (Scope of Work), page 8; Section 4.5.1 (Key Personnel � Position and Function), page 11. Question 3 � Anticipated TDY Headcount Beyond the Standing Detachment (Rephrased from: "Beyond the standing detachment of up to eight (8) Marines, what are the typical and maximum numbers of TDY personnel...") Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services) confirms the Contractor shall provide food services for up to eight (8) MSG personnel and shall accommodate additional Temporary Duty (TDY) personnel at no additional cost to the Government. For planning purposes, Offerors should anticipate a not-to-exceed range of up to four (4) additional TDY personnel during surge periods, beyond the standing eight-person detachment. Because this solicitation is for food preparation services only � and not the procurement of ingredients or supplies, which remains a separate Government-managed process under Section 1 (Prices) � any increase in MSG personnel supported during TDY periods, up to this maximum, will not result in additional cost to the Contractor. Offerors should build sufficient flexibility into portioning and menu planning to accommodate periodic increases above the standing detachment. Solicitation citations: Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services), page 9; Section 1 (Prices), page 5. Question 4 � Existence of a Budgetary Ceiling for Ingredient Purchases (Rephrased from: "As the Government purchases ingredients from the contractor's weekly shopping list, is there a budgetary ceiling, per-person allowance, or historical monthly spend...") The solicitation does not establish a fixed budgetary ceiling or per-person ingredient allowance. Per Section 1 (Prices), the Contractor provides a weekly ingredient shopping list, which the Government (through the Marines) purchases and delivers to the MSGR. This is a Government-managed process separate from the Contractor's firm-fixed monthly price for labor and services. No historical monthly spend figures are being released as part of this solicitation. Solicitation citations: Section 1 (Prices), page 5. Question 5 � Confirmation of Set-Aside Status (Rephrased from: "Could you please confirm the set-aside status of this acquisition...") This acquisition is unrestricted. No set-aside applies, per Block 10 of the SF-1449. Solicitation citations: SF-1449, Block 10, page 3. Question 6 � Applicability of the Section 5000C Excise Tax (Rephrased from: "Please confirm whether the 2% excise tax under 26 U.S.C. 5000C applies to this award, or whether a treaty-based exemption may be claimed...") Per the Zadroga Act notice in Section 1 and Provision 52.229-11 in Section 5, payments under this contract may be subject to the 2% excise tax under 26 U.S.C. 5000C unless the Offeror is a U.S. person or qualifies for an exemption. The Netherlands currently maintains an income tax treaty with the United States that may provide a basis for exemption from this excise tax. However, regardless of treaty eligibility, any foreign-person Offeror seeking to claim an exemption must still submit a completed IRS Form W-14 with its quotation. If the form is not submitted, the Government will withhold the full 2% from each payment, per FAR 52.229-11(e)(2). Solicitation citations: Section 1 (Zadroga Act Notice), page 5; Section 5, Provision 52.229-11(e)(2), pages 52�53. Question 7 � Confirmation of Weekday-Only Meal Service (No Weekend Coverage) (Rephrased from: "Please confirm whether any weekend (Saturday/Sunday) coverage is expected...") Per PWS �1.2.2 and Attachment 1, meal service is scheduled Monday through Friday, 0700�1800 hours, on a 20-weekday menu cycle. The solicitation does not require any weekend (Saturday/Sunday) coverage. Service is limited strictly to the five weekday service periods described in the meal service schedule. Solicitation citations: PWS �1.2.2, page 8; Attachment 1, page 22. Question 8 � Nationality and Work-Authorization Eligibility of the Proposed Cook (Rephrased from: "Could the Government clarify whether the position may be filled by a Third Country National (TCN), or whether it must be a local national or EU/Netherlands-authorized worker?") The U.S. Government does not provide guidance, direction, or assistance regarding the nationality classification (e.g., Third Country National, local national, or otherwise) of Contractor personnel. Ensuring that all personnel hold valid host-nation work authorization and any required licenses or permits is the sole responsibility of the Contractor, consistent with Attachment 1 (Licensing, Laws, and Regulations) and Clause 652.242-73 (Authorization and Performance). Solicitation citations: Section 4.4.1 (Personnel Security), page 12; Attachment 1 (Licensing, Laws, and Regulations), page 20; Clause 652.242-73 (Authorization and Performance), page 43. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Geospatial Intelligence Processing and Exploitation (GeoPEX) BAA NUMBER: BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 SEP 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 SEP 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY22 � 30 Sep 2021 FY23 � 30 Sep 2022 FY24 � 30 Sep 2023 FY25 � 30 Sep 2024 FY26 � 30 Sep 2025 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the Beta SAM website at https://beta.SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking white papers for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to provide geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) in all its forms and from whatever source - imagery, imagery intelligence, or geospatial data and information - to ensure a solid foundation of knowledge for planning, decision, and action while creating tailored, customer-specific geospatial intelligence, analytic services, and solutions. This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-17-S-7004 Knowledge Aided GEOINT Latency Reduction (KAGLR) BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 24 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $250K to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Bernard J. Clarke AFRL/RIGD 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-2106 Email: Bernard.Clarke@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below: Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. Please submit your offer via email to ManilaPurchasing@state.gov prior to the response date and time. It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; in MS-Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 10MB. If the file size should exceed the 10MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 10MB each.

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice and Pre-Solicitation Meeting/Industry Day announcement for Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS)
description: **** Update as of 08 OCT 2020, the Tech Read Library Instructions have been updated to allow for a digital copy for review by potential Small Business Offerors. Please see below the attached updated instructions to obtain access to the Tech Read Library. The name of the document is C-sUAS Digital Tech Read Library_Instr_20201006. **** **** Update as of 28 AUG 2020, the Government's Acquisition Strategy has been approved and it has been determined that this effort will be solicited as a Small Business set-aside under NAICS 541715 Aircraft, Aircraft Engine and Engine Parts exception with size standard of 1,500 employees. Please continue to watch this posting for updates until the solicitation is released. **** ****Updated 27 AUG 2020, Posted Corrected Version of Industry Day Q&A Responses.**** ****Updated 24 AUG 2020, Posted Industry Day Q&A Responses.**** ****Updated 18 MAR 2020, Due to the COVID-19 spread and site closure the Technical Read Library Access is currently suspended until at least 11 MAY 2020. Please note that depending on the state of things this date can be pushed out further or rescined earlier.**** ****Updated 13 FEB 2020, Posted an Updated version of the Industry Day Attendees List**** ****Updated 6 FEB 2020, Posted Releasable Industry Day Slides, Industry Day Attendees List, DRAFT Version of Umbrella SOW, DRAFT Version of Task Order 1 Work Description, and Updated Tech Read Library Instructions**** ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. Evaluation of the capability packages received in response to the Request for Information (RFI-RIKD-19-01) resulted in a determination that a small business set-aside could be established. A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for this effort is anticipated to be released during the 1st quarter of CY 2020. Potential Offerors will be encouraged to review and comment on the Draft RFP, including the Statement of Work (SOW) and Sections L and M. Please monitor this notice for updates. THE ENTIRE SOLICITATION WILL BE ISSUED ON THE BETA SAM WEBSITE AT https://beta.sam.gov/. Paper copies will not be available. The solicitation and any amendments thereto will only be available by downloading the documents from the website. All prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring the site for the release of amendments (if any) or other information pertaining to the solicitation. It is anticipated that the website will provide a registration service that will send an e-mail notification when a change is made to the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the RFP which shall be considered. Based on market research, the Government is not using FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, to solicit for the described supplies or services. However, interested parties may identify to the Contracting Officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item(s) within thirty (30) days of this notice. Technical questions should be directed to the Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR), Donna Toole at (315) 330-3972, donna.toole.1@us.af.mil. Any contractual questions or questions concerning this Presolicitation Notice should be communicated directly to the Contract Specialist, Matthew Zawisza at (315) 330-4922, matthew.zawisza@us.af.mil, or the Contracting Officer, Terrence Lipinski at (315) 330-4510, terrence.lipinski@us.af.mil. In accordance with AFFARS 5301.91, an Ombudsman has been appointed to hear and facilitate the resolution of concerns from offerors, potential offerors, and others for this acquisition. Before consulting with an Ombudsman, interested parties must first address their concerns, issues, disagreements, and/or recommendations to the Contracting Officer, Terrence Lipinski at (315) 330-4510, terrence.lipinski@us.af.mil, for resolution. AFFARS clause 5352.201-9101, Ombudsman, will be incorporated into the resultant contract. When requested, the Ombudsman will maintain strict confidentiality as to the source of the concern. The existence of the Ombudsman does not affect the authority of the Program Manager, Contracting Officer, or source selection official. Further, the Ombudsman does not participate in the evaluation of proposals, the source selection process, or the adjudication of protests or formal contract disputes. The Ombudsman may refer the party to another official who can resolve the concern. Consulting an Ombudsman does not alter or postpone the timelines for any other processes (e.g., agency level bid protests, GAO bid protests, requests for debriefings, employee-employer actions, contests of OMB Circular A-76 competition performance decisions). If resolution cannot be made by the Contracting Officer, concerned parties may contact the following AFRL Ombudsman: Mr. Steven L. Ewers, 1864 Fourth Street, Wright-Patterson AFB OH 45433-7130, COMM (937) 904-4407, email: steven.ewers@us.af.mil. Concerns, issues, disagreements, and recommendations that cannot be resolved at the AFRL level may be brought by the concerned party for further consideration to the Air Force Ombudsman, Associate Deputy

title: Base Operation Support (BOS) Services for Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Laurel Bay (LB), Laurel Bay Schools, Beaufort, South Carolina, and Townsend Bombing Range Shellman Bluff, Georgia
description: This is not a request for either a quote or proposal, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to notify potential offerors of Base Operation Support (BOS), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Performance-Based contract with Recurring and Non-Recurring services to provide Facility Investment, Pest Control, Electrical and Base Support Vehicle and Equipment (BSVE) services for Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Laurel Bay (LB), Laurel Bay Schools, Beaufort, South Carolina, Townsend Bombing Range Shellman Bluff, Georgia, and outlying areas supported by the installations. The Contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, material and equipment facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide BOS services. Locations include but are not limited to: Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Laurel Bay (LB), Laurel Bay Schools, Beaufort, South Carolina, Townsend Bombing Range Shellman Bluff, Georgia, and outlying areas supported by the installations. General Work Requirements: Sub-Annex 1502000 Facility Investment The intent of Facility Investment is to specify the requirements for Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) sub-functions only. The Facility Investment requirements within this sub-annex primarily consist of infrastructure sustainment and minimal restoration and modernization work. Sustainment is the maintenance and repair necessary to keep an inventory of facilities and other assets in good working order. Restoration and modernization normally consists of major rehabilitation and capital improvements that is accomplished through other USMC programs. Some major repair, minor construction and stand-alone demolition may be accomplished as part of Facility Investment. The Contractor shall perform maintenance, repair, alteration, demolition and minor construction for the following: Building and Structures � to include interior and exterior finishes, plumbing (includes backflow prevention devices), grease traps, roofing, foundation, structural components, cathodic protection systems, tanks, POL system, pipelines, relamping, converters, Building Systems -HVAC, Direct Digital Control (DDC), Emergency Management Control System (EMCS), Vertical Transportation Equipment (VTE), intrusion detection systems, bridge and jib cranes, boilers, Unfired Pressure Vessels (UPV), compressed air systems, potable water (including backflow prevention devices), wastewater, and electrical. Sub-Annex 1503020 Pest Control The contractor shall provide pest control services to prevent and control nuisance, structural, turf and ornamental, and medical arthropod and vertebrate pests, including but not limited to cockroaches, termites, ants, fleas, bed bugs, silverfish, stored product pests, mosquitoes, mice, rats, bats, feral dogs and cats and other vertebrates, bees, wasps, pigeons, and nuisance birds. Sub-Annex 1602000 Electrical The Contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, material, and equipment to continuously operate, maintain, and repair the electrical power generation plant, transmission systems and distribution systems. The intent is to specify the requirements for electrical power generation, power transmission and distribution. All sources for generating electrical power for utilities, e.g., boilers, wind, solar, gas, etc. Annex 1700000 Base Support Vehicle and Equipment The intent of BSVE is to specify the requirements for a transportation program consisting of vehicles, equipment maintenance and repairs. The vehicle and equipment operations shall include dispatch, Weight Handling Equipment (WHE) / Material Handling Equipment (MHE), Ordinance Handling Equipment (OHE), liquid movements, people movements, operator licensing and training, inspection and certification, and specified administrative program management. Source Selection procedures will be used to select the best value offeror using tradeoff analysis in accordance with FAR Part 15 � Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the Request for Proposal (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. The offeror�s proposal shall contain a response to each of the evaluation factors and shall be in the form prescribed by the solicitation. The solicitation requires the evaluation of price and the following non-price factors: Factor 1 � Management Approach, Factor 2 � Corporate Experience, Factor 3 � Safety, and Factor 4 � Past Performance. Factor 2 Corporate Experience and Factor 4 Past Performance: The distinction between corporate experience and past performance is that experience pertains to the volume of work completed by a contractor that are comparable to the types of work described under the definition of recent, relevant projects, in terms of size, scope, and complexity. Past performance pertains to both the relevance of recent efforts and how well a contractor has performed on the contracts. Size: A contract with a yearly value of at least $4,900,000 for recurring services. Scope/Complexity: Offeror must have provided all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide Facility Investment, Pest Control, Electrical, and BSVE as described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). NOTE: An Unacceptable rating in any of the non-cost/price factors will result in an overall rating of Unacceptable for the non-cost/price factors, unless corrected through discussions. The proposed procurement will be issued as a NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic BOS, Indefinite Delivery, /Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) type contract with recurring and non-recurring services. The IDIQ contract will include online ordering capability using FedMall for the Non-Recurring Exhibit Line Item Numbers (ELINs). Acceptance of Government Purchase Credit Cards is required along with the purchase of FedMall Encrypted software. The North American Classification System (NAICS) is 561210; the size standard is $47M. Offers shall be submitted for the performance of work for a period of one year. However, the initial term of the contract may be for a period of less than one year. The Government has the option to extend the term of the contract services for additional periods of one to twelve months. The contract will be for a base period of one (1) year, with six (6) one-year option periods, and one (1) six-month period, not to exceed sixty-six (90) months. This contract will include a 60-day phase-in period. The proposed procurement will be listed as a competitive 100% 8(a) Small business set-aside. The Request for Proposal (RFP) will be made available in electronic format only (Adobe Acrobat (pdf)) and will be posted on SAM.gov website on or about 18 May 2026. The estimated proposal due date shall be at least 30 days after the RFP is posted. (Contractors - inquiries must be submitted in writing to Krystal Goodman at (krystal.s.goodman2.civ@us.navy.mil) at least 10 days prior to the RFP due date. The SAM site address is https://sam.gov/. Notifications of any updates or amendments to the solicitation will be posted on the SAM. Contractors are encouraged to register on the SAM website. Only registered contractors will be notified by e-mail when amendments to the solicitation are issued. IT IS THE SOLE RESPONISBILITY OF THE OFFEROR TO CONTINUALLY VIEW THE WEBSITE FOR CHANGES. All prospective contractors are required to register on the System for Award Management (SAM) database. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the Internet at https://sam.gov/. This contract will replace a contract for similar services. The current contract is N4008518D9738, for BOS Services for Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS)

description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE/PROPOSAL: The National Park Service intends to solicit a quote and enter into a contract with Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc located at 1550 Industrial PKWY, Brunswick, Ohio 44212-2349, United States. This requirement is for the repair of the rotary manifold for a John Deere 85G Excavator which requires removal, inspection and reconditioning for Cuyahoga Valley National Park. Murphy Tractor is the only John Deere Certified Dealer that is close to the park in Cleveland/ Akron and the surrounding areas. The rotary manifold assembly (10-port configuration) and associated seal kits are proprietary components designed to OEM specifications. Compatibility, warranty protection, and operational integrity necessitate procurement of John Deere-approved parts and qualified service support. Substituting non-OEM components may compromise system performance, increase failure risk, and create liability exposure. If the park outsourced this requirement to another Certified John Deere Dealer that is further away this would add excessive additional cost for reassembly of the machine and due to transportation costs. Additionally, this equipment must be urgently repaired in order to support park operations for the maintenance of park railroad tracks which could be impeded due to mudslide or other hazards. Failure to repair this equipment in a timely manner could endanger park staff and guests. Due to the above, sole-sourcing to Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc ensures the most expedient and compliant resolution to these urgent repairs. Questions may be directed to Ryan R Begany in writing by email to ryan_begany@ios.doi.gov. NO PHONE inquiries will be accepted.

This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-17-S-7004 Knowledge Aided GEOINT Latency Reduction (KAGLR) BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 24 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $250K to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. title: GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses Industry Day
description: Special Notice Title of Event: GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses Industry Day Audience: Industry Representatives When: 7 April 2026, 0800-1600 Where: Air Force Metrology & Calibration (AFMETCAL) and the Air Force Primary Standards Laboratory (AFPSL), 813 Irving-Wick Dr. W., Heath, OH 43056 Abstract: The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is hosting an Industry Day to provide information and gather feedback regarding the potential modification of the GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses. This event is critical for potential offerors to gain a comprehensive understanding of the current system and the specific requirements for its modification. The potential modification of the MD8060 would include removing the current hydraulic and electronic systems then installing a manually controlled hydraulic pump that maintains the MD8060�s accuracy of �0.025% rdg and range from 200 to 60,000 lbf. The primary objective of this Industry Day is to allow industry partners the opportunity to inspect the MD8060 firsthand at Air Force Primary Standards Lab (AFPSL). This on-site inspection is essential for understanding the requirement and developing an informed and effective solution. We encourage industry to identify potential risks and propose mitigation strategies related to the system modification. Potential offerors on any future solicitation are required to inspect the MD8060 on site, as they likely would not be able to submit a competitive proposal without a site visit. In no event shall failure to inspect the MD8060 on site constitute grounds for a claim after any resulting contract award. Objectives: Provide early engagement and communication to Industry Provide a forum to discuss modification strategies Improve the quality of any future solicitation Identify vendors interested and capable of executing modification of the MD8060 Who Should Attend? Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Industry Day event. For this Industry Day, the Government will permit a maximum of three (3) individuals per vendor to register and attend. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code to be used for this procurement is 334516 (Laboratory Analytical Instruments Manufacturing). Items for Discussion: To facilitate effective exchange, the Government requests questions in writing prior to the Industry Day. This will allow the Government to conduct research in advance of scheduled one-on-one sessions and come prepared to answer your questions. Please submit your specific questions to BOTH frank.capuano@us.af.mil and thomas.carson.2@us.af.mil. Answers may be limited as the Government is in the Market Research phase. The Government is not requesting capability statements or briefings at this time. Scheduled one-on-one sessions will allow interested vendors the opportunity to openly communicate with the Government by providing comments and inputs for consideration during the development of the solicitation. Times for the one-on-one sessions will be scheduled and communicated with registered attendees prior to the Industry Day. Sessions will be no more than 60 minutes and discussion will focus on the MD8060 requirements. In the event an interested party cannot attend on the scheduled date, an alternate date for a site visit will be accommodated as necessary to ensure maximum participation. To ensure transparency, non-proprietary questions and answers will be recorded, sanitized, and placed on SAM.gov. Please e-mail proposed topics and questions that you may have no later than 27 March 2026. Registration: Pre-registration is MANDATORY for attendance. Please submit the following information electronically to BOTH frank.capuano@us.af.mil and thomas.carson.2@us.af.mil no later than 2:00 PM EDT 27 March 2026 to pre-register. Information addressing security, directions, and individual session times will be provided to respondents. For this Industry Day, the Government will permit a maximum of three (3) individuals per vendor to register and attend. Only group registrations will be processed. The following information shall be provided for each attendee: 1. Individual attendees' full name and title 2. Individual attendees' e-mail address 3. Company name 4. Company Cage Code 5. Small Business Status 6. Telephone number 7. Visitor request form (To be provided upon notice of pre-registration) 7. Do you wish to have your company name included on a published list of attendees? Additional Information: Any submitted information may be used to structure future solicitations. Sensitive, proprietary, or otherwise confidential information must be marked appropriately in the response. Information received from respondents will not be shared with other vendors. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the market research. Additionally, information gathered through this meeting may influence RFQ development. This notification does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation, award a contract, or conduct an acquisition in any particular way. The U.S. Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement or incurred for participation in the Industry Day will NOT be reimbursed. All information marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded to prevent disclosure to non-Government personnel and entities. The acquisition strategy for the modification of the GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses has not been finalized; this requirement is in the market research and planning phase. No solicitation or projected solicitation date is available at this time. Points of Contact: All communication regarding this solicitation should be sent to BOTH of the following individuals: Thomas Carson, Contracting Officer thomas.carson.2@us.af.mil 937-713-5844 Frank Capuano, Contract Specialist frank.capuano@us.af.mil 937-713-5842

These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. title: J--Excavator Repair - CUVA
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF AWARD FOR A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE: The National Park Service is awarding Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc located at 1550 Industrial PKWY, Brunswick, Ohio 44212-2349, United States; a large business, the contract to provide the Excavator Repairs service requirement for Cuyahoga Valley National Park, which is being purchased for $15,826.74. Please see attached justification document for more details. This requirement is for the repair of the rotary manifold for a John Deere 85G Excavator which requires removal, inspection and reconditioning for Cuyahoga Valley National Park. Murphy Tractor is the only John Deere Certified Dealer that is close to the park in Cleveland/ Akron and the surrounding areas. The rotary manifold assembly (10-port configuration) and associated seal kits are proprietary components designed to OEM specifications. Compatibility, warranty protection, and operational integrity necessitate procurement of John Deere-approved parts and qualified service support. Substituting non-OEM components may compromise system performance, increase failure risk, and create liability exposure. If the park outsourced this requirement to another Certified John Deere Dealer that is further away this would add excessive additional cost for reassembly of the machine and due to transportation costs. Additionally, this equipment must be urgently repaired in order to support park operations for the maintenance of park railroad tracks which could be impeded due to mudslide or other hazards. Failure to repair this equipment in a timely manner could endanger park staff and guests. Due to the above, sole-sourcing to Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc ensures the most expedient and compliant resolution to these urgent repairs. Questions may be directed to Ryan R Begany in writing by email to ryan_begany@ios.doi.gov. NO PHONE inquiries will be accepted.

title: PSXE242022 Repair Facility Exterior Lighting
description: Invitation for Bids (IFB) Set-Aside for Small Businesses NAICS Code: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction The Tennessee National Guard intends to issue an Invitation for Bids to award a single firm fixed-price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the repair of the Repair Facility Exterior Lighting at McGhee Tyson Air National Guard Base, Tennessee. The work includes, but is not limited to, replace existing facility lighting control system by repairing existing exterior lighting with new LED fixtures, control modules, and various lighting components. The contractor is to provide a complete and useable system in accordance with the plans and specifications. The contract duration will be 365 calendar days after the notice to proceed, to include inspection and punch list. This project is set aside 100% for Small Businesses. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. The magnitude of construction is between $500,000 and $1,500,000. The tentative date for issuing the solicitation is on-or-about 15 July 2026. The tentative date for the pre-bid conference is on-or-about 24 July 2026, 10:00 AM local time, at 320 Post Ave, Louisville, Tennessee, 37777. Interested contractors are encouraged to attend and shall follow conference registration and base access requirements shown in the solicitation. A site visit will follow the pre-bid conference. All questions for the pre-bid conference must be submitted via email to Lisa.Fingland@us.af.mil. The bid opening date is tentatively planned for on-or-about 17 August 2026. Interested offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for award. To register, go to www.SAM.gov. The solicitation and associated information will be available only from the Contract Opportunities page at SAM.gov. Your attention is directed to FAR clause 52.219-14, LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING, which states that for General Construction, the prime contractor will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. In accordance with FAR 36.211(b), the following information is provided: (1) The National Guard has no agency-specific policies or procedures applicable to the definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts other than those described at FAR 43.204 and DFARS 243.204. title: Global Distribution Expeditionary Contract
description: Update - Redacted Justification and Approval added to special notice. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) anticipates awarding a modification to existing DLA Distribution Contract SP3300-21-D-5002 on a sole source basis to Olgoonik Federal, LLC. This contract provides labor to support workload surges, unforeseen/unplanned workload, contingency operations and special projects. The modification would increase the ceiling amount as the contract has been outpacing the anticipated spend rate. Pursuant to the exception under FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii), only Olgoonik Federal, LLC is capable of providing the services at this time; award to any other source will result in unacceptable delays and would preclude DLA from reacting timely to requirements. This action could not have been overcome by advanced planning given the nature of this contract, which is to support unplanned, unforeseen requirements. If the contract ceiling is not increased to accommodate the known and anticipated requirements of this contract, as well as any unplanned requirements, DLA Distribution would not have a contract vehicle to provide services within the scope of this contract to support DLA and its customers mission. The modification to current contract SP3300-21-D-5002 will serve as a temporary solution to fulfill immediate mission requirements. A follow-on procurement is in process. The justification and approval for this ceiling increase will be posted as part of this notice once executed. This is not a solicitation for proposals or an invitation for bids. The Government does not anticipate receiving responses to this notice of a non-competitive action.

The Work includes but is not limited to partial removal and disposal of an existing concrete dam and headgate structure comprised of concrete, rock, rebar, regrading of the North Fork Virgin River for a distance of approximately 300 feet, construction of a new intake structure including a fish screen, removal and disposal of approximately 275� of existing CMP pipe and concrete manhole, installation of approximately 285� of 18�� ADS N-12 pipe (approximately 40� to be placed within 24�� CMP pipe), removal of a concrete turnout box, reseating of an existing 12� flume, approximately 150 feet of boulder embankment rip rap and (Option 1) installation of approximately 350� of smart ditch SOLICITATION NUMBER: 140P6426B0008 PROJECT MAGNITUDE: Between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000 TYPE OF CONTRACT: This will be a firm-fixed price contract expected to be awarded to a prime contractor by August 2026 with performance to begin in October 2026. Construction Wage Rate Requirements for Washington County, UT will apply. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) CODE CLASSIFICATION and SET ASIDE: The NAICS Code is 237990, and the size standard is $45 million. This project is set aside 100% for Total Small Businesses. SITE VISIT: A site visit date, time, and meeting location will be announced in the solicitation. Offerors are highly encouraged to attend the scheduled site visit to inspect the site and to ensure they fully understand the requirement and conditions that may affect the cost of the project, specifications, and performance. PUBLICIZING: The official solicitation and its attachments will be issued and available in May 2026 and will be posted to the Contract Opportunities/SAM.gov website at https://sam.gov/content/opportunities . The contracting office will not provide hardcopies or email copies of the solicitation. REGISTRATIONS: In order to be awarded a contract, an offeror must have an UEI number. Also, the offeror must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM), website at http://www.sam.gov, and have completed their Online Representations and Certifications at the time of the solicitation close date once the solicitation is posted. POINT OF CONTACT: Christopher Bauer, Contracting Officer, christopher_bauer@ios.doi.gov, 330-468-2500 x5.

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice and Pre-Solicitation Meeting/Industry Day announcement for Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS)
description: ****Updated 6 FEB 2020, Posted Releasable Industry Day Slides, Industry Day Attendees List, DRAFT Version of Umbrella SOW, DRAFT Version of Task Order 1 Work Description, and Updated Tech Read Library Instructions**** ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. Evaluation of the capability packages received in response to the Request for Information (RFI-RIKD-19-01) resulted in a determination that a small business set-aside could be established. A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for this effort is anticipated to be released during the 1st quarter of CY 2020. Potential Offerors will be encouraged to review and comment on the Draft RFP, including the Statement of Work (SOW) and Sections L and M. Please monitor this notice for updates. THE ENTIRE SOLICITATION WILL BE ISSUED ON THE BETA SAM WEBSITE AT https://beta.sam.gov/. Paper copies will not be available. The solicitation and any amendments thereto will only be available by downloading the documents from the website. All prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring the site for the release of amendments (if any) or other information pertaining to the solicitation. It is anticipated that the website will provide a registration service that will send an e-mail notification when a change is made to the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the RFP which shall be considered. Based on market research, the Government is not using FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, to solicit for the described supplies or services. However, interested parties may identify to the Contracting Officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item(s) within thirty (30) days of this notice. Technical questions should be directed to the Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR), Donna Toole at (315) 330-3972, donna.toole.1@us.af.mil. Any contractual questions or questions concerning this Presolicitation Notice should be communicated directly to the Contract Specialist, Matthew Zawisza at (315) 330-4922, matthew.zawisza@us.af.mil, or the Contracting Officer, Terrence Lipinski at (315) 330-4510, terrence.lipinski@us.af.mil. title: GEOSPATIAL INTELLIGENCE PROCESSING AND EXPLOITATION (GeoPEX)
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Geospatial Intelligence Processing and Exploitation (GeoPEX) BAA NUMBER: BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 SEP 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 SEP 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY22 � 30 Sep 2021 FY23 � 30 Sep 2022 FY24 � 30 Sep 2023 FY25 � 30 Sep 2024 FY26 � 30 Sep 2025 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the Beta SAM website at https://beta.SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking white papers for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to provide geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) in all its forms and from whatever source - imagery, imagery intelligence, or geospatial data and information - to ensure a solid foundation of knowledge for planning, decision, and action while creating tailored, customer-specific geospatial intelligence, analytic services, and solutions. This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-17-S-7004 Knowledge Aided GEOINT Latency Reduction (KAGLR) BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 24 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $250K to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Bernard J. Clarke AFRL/RIGD 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-2106 Email: Bernard.Clarke@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below: Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. PLEASE SEE THE ATTACHED GEOPEX SYNOPSIS v12.doc AMENDMENT 1 to BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 The purpose of this amendment to BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 is to update the mailing instructions in Section IV.3.c to remove the requirement for a hard copy to be mailed. The updated mailing instructions are below: Part II, Section IV.3.c. is updated as follows: c. MAILING INSTRUCTIONS. Email Unclassified electronic submission to the TPOC identified in Section VII. Contractors will be required to provide documentation of their Security Program Plan for initial Institution S&T Protection Program Review. The purpose of requesting the plan is to evaluate the offeror�s capacity for protecting the Government�s S&T and failure to demonstrate a plan adequate to meet the needs of the requirement may be grounds for considering the proposal unawardable. The Government will be only required to provide a general statement of the reasoning due to Government OPSEC measures. After award, the Contractor/Recipient will be required to re-submit the Standard Form 424 as an annual requirement to the points of contact listed above. No other changes are made.

title: FY26 City Pair Program Award
description: This procurement is for scheduled certificated U.S. airlines to provide passenger transportation services, Government-wide, for over 16,000 domestic/international airport or city pairs. The requirement-type contracts will be for one year beginning October 1, 2025, plus one 2-month option period and one 1-month option period. The contracts are for the movement of passengers and are used by almost all Federal Agencies and various other authorized users. Travel agent services will not be solicited under this solicitation. Prior to award, air carriers must be approved by the Department of Defense (DOD), as well as have the appropriate Federal Aviation Administration certification. Carriers who are otherwise eligible must also participate in the Civil Reserve Air Fleet (CRAF) program or receive a Letter of CRAF Technical Ineligibility from the United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM). For information regarding the CRAF program, call the DOD Commercial Airlift Division at (618) 229-4801. The FY26 City Pair Program has awarded items to 7 carriers: Alaska Airlines, American Airlines, Breeze Airways, Delta Air Lines, JetBlue Airways, Southwest Airlines and United Airlines.

title: P309 Replace School Age Care Centers Camp Foster and Camp McTureous, Okinawa Japan
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE W912HV26BA007 FY26 MCN P309, School Age Care Centers Replacement Camp Foster and McTureous, Okinawa, Japan The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Japan District (POJ) is providing a PRE-SOLICITATION notice pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 5.101(a) (https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul) for an upcoming Invitation for Bid (IFB). This is not a solicitation. PROJECT INFORMATION Project Title: FY26 MCN P309, School Age Care Centers Replacement Project Location: Camp Foster and McTureous, Okinawa, Japan Product Service Code (PSC): Y1AZ - CONSTRUCTION OF OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE FACILITIES AND SERVICE BUILDINGS NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Project Magnitude: Between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000 (Between �3,479,087,500 and �7,522,075,000) Project(s) Description: Construct low-rise reinforced concrete structures to replace the current School Age Care Centers (SACC) located on Camp Foster (Building 1) and Camp McTureous (Building 2). The functional areas will include spaces for the lobby, reception, activity rooms, a large kitchen, restrooms, a multi-purpose half-court room without bleachers, a janitor room, administrative offices, a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics)/computer room, and storage rooms. Exterior requirements will include benches, fencing, and a children's drop-off/pick-up waiting area. Construct an outdoor playground area next to SAC at each site. It should include energy-absorbing poured flooring and age-appropriate playground equipment. Facility-related control systems include cybersecurity features following current Department of Defense (DoD) criteria. Estimated Period of Performance: 1032 Calendar Days SOLICITATION INFORMATION: 1. Procurement Method: The Government will issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) solicitation. 2. The Government anticipates issuing the solicitation in July 2026. The solicitation, when issued, will identify the site visit date, RFI and bid submission due dates. description: The Naval Information Warfare Systems Command (NAVWAR) in support of the Tactical Data Link (TDL) Program Office (formerly Multifunctional Information Distribution (MIDS) Program Office (MPO)) plans to issue a Full and Open Competitive Request for Proposal (RFP) for the development and procurement of National Security Agency (NSA) certified MIDS Weapons Data Link (WDL) Small Weapons Attritable (SWARMM) Family 3 (SF3) Radios.
